messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@ajaxstream.com>

Cc: sophie.lin@ajaxstream.com, oncall@ajaxstream.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput collapse + 5xx spike - urgent

Diego —

We're seeing a sudden throughput collapse across our EU region traffic hitting your hosted API. Error rates jumped from ~0.5% to 12% around 07:45 PT and tail latency has spiked to ~3s p50. End users are seeing timeouts and our retry rates are producing large bursts on the backend.

Attached is a short log extract and a couple of traces from our end (ajax_error_sample.log). Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (deploys, model rollouts, routing)? We have an event at 09:00 PT with our leadership and need a quick readout.

This is impacting our checkout flow — we need a mitigation path and ETA.

— Alex
Director, Platform
AjaxStream

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden throughput collapse + 5xx spike - urgent

On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 08:20 AM, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — looping you in. AjaxStream reports a sudden throughput collapse and 5xx spike from ~07:45 PT.

Quick summary from infra: no control-plane deploys during 07:00–08:30 PT. We did have an automated model variant rollout that completed at 07:40 PT for the 'conversational-lite-v2' family in eu-west-1; it's a staggered variant swap that should be backward compatible but does change kernel selection.

Telemetry shows a correlation between the rollout completion and a KV-cache eviction storm on a subset of serving hosts (10% of hosts saw >5x cache miss rate for hot prefixes). That + retry amplification from AjaxStream's client appears to have overwhelmed per-host token production causing p50/p95 latency spikes and an uptick in 500-level failures upstream.

Immediate actionable items I can do now:
- Roll back the variant swap for AjaxStream traffic (if we can pin them to prior model id) — low-risk and immediate.
- Temporarily enable prefix caching sticky routing for AjaxStream (reduces cache misses).
- Throttle downstream retries via a short-lived rate-limit rule (we should coordinate with AjaxStream on client-side backoff).

I'll stand by on the bridge and can run rollback in <10m if we confirm pinning.

-Hannah
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime

Attachment: infra-rollout-events-20270622.txt (stub)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Alex / Sophie — thanks for the quick heads up and log sample. We're assembling an immediate mitigation plan and will keep this thread as the single source of truth for exec updates.

Short status for your leadership call:
- Incident: increased 5xx rate and latency in eu-west-1 starting ~07:45 PT, impacting AjaxStream checkout traffic.
- Root-candidate: recent variant rollout for 'conversational-lite-v2' correlated with KV-cache eviction spike on ~10% of serving hosts.
- Immediate mitigations being prepared now: rollback of variant for AjaxStream traffic; enable sticky routing for hot prefixes; temporary retry throttling.
- ETA for first mitigation (pin to prior model): ~15 minutes after you confirm tolerance for a short pin (no code change required).

Ask for AjaxStream: please apply exponential backoff on retries for 10–30 minutes while we stabilize; it will materially reduce amplification. We'll send a short exec summary once we have successful mitigation.

We will open a dedicated bridge and share a one-page executive summary to hand to your leadership.

— Marissa
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@ajaxstream.com>, Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@ajaxstream.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive one-pager: AjaxStream stability event (summary & next steps)

Alex / Sophie —

Below is an executive summary you can share with your leadership. We're keeping it concise and operational:

Executive summary — AjaxStream stability event (2027-06-22)
- Impact: Elevated 5xx rate and tail latency for AjaxStream traffic in eu-west-1 between ~07:45–08:10 PT. Customer-visible impact: failed checkout attempts; increased timeouts.
- Root cause (candidate): Automated model variant rollout for 'conversational-lite-v2' completed at 07:40 PT; the new kernel selection triggered KV-cache evictions on a subset of hosts. Cache miss amplification combined with aggressive client retries produced elevated per-host load and 500 responses.
- Actions taken:
  * Immediately pinned AjaxStream traffic to previous model variant at 08:02 PT (rollback completed).
  * Enabled sticky routing for hot prefixes and increased KV-cache retention thresholds on affected hosts.
  * Coordinated with AjaxStream to reduce client-side retries during stabilization window (08:00–08:20 PT).
- Outcome: By 08:12 PT system telemetry shows error rates returned to baseline (<1%) and p95 latency reduced under SLA targets. No data loss or user data exposure.
- Next steps / postmortem scope:
  * Full root-cause analysis on variant rollout detection and cache eviction thresholds.
  * Improve rollout targeting to avoid variant swaps on high-QPS customers during peak windows.
  * Implement an automatic short-circuit: on cache-eviction storms, temporarily pin traffic to prior variant and notify customers automatically.
  * Deliver a joint RCA and timeline by 2027-06-24 COB.

Attachments: I attached a short exec-friendly PDF (redwood-exec-summary.pdf) for your leadership meeting. If you'd like, Laura and I can join the post-call to walk through the timeline.

We're treating this as priority and will keep the bridge open until your team confirms stability.

Best,
Diego
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-exec-summary.pdf (1-page, executive view)
